sentence: Losartan is a medicine for high blood pressure, and it belongs to the group called angiotensin II receptor blockers.
note: NHS: losartan is a medicine for high blood pressure.

sentence: The NHS says it can also be used for some people with heart failure and for kidney problems linked to type 2 diabetes.
note: About page summary: used for high blood pressure, heart failure and kidney problems in diabetes (search summary; not quoted in detail).

sentence: It is available on prescription only, as tablets or a liquid that is swallowed.
note: NHS pages describe tablets and liquid; prescription medicine. Regulatory status also in existing record.

sentence: Losartan blocks the effect of a hormone called angiotensin II, which narrows blood vessels.
note: NHS/MedlinePlus describe it as an angiotensin II receptor blocker; mechanism also in existing page.

sentence: With the hormone blocked, blood vessels relax and blood pressure falls.
note: As above.

sentence: The NHS explains that the prescriber decides the amount and timing, and that people are usually asked to keep taking it even when they feel well.
note: Common questions/how to take pages: keep taking even if you feel well (search summary only partly returned).

sentence: It can be taken with or without food.
note: NHS how-and-when page: may be taken with or without food (search summary).

sentence: The NHS lists dizziness and tiredness as common side effects, and these are more likely when starting treatment or after the amount is raised.
note: Side effects page: dizziness and tiredness common; dizziness likelier at start or after a bigger dose.

sentence: Headaches are also common, and they usually fade after the first week.
note: Side effects page: headaches usually go after first week.

sentence: The NHS says a person who feels dizzy or tired should not drive or use tools.
note: Search summary: should not affect driving unless dizzy or tired.

sentence: Long-term use can sometimes make the kidneys work less well, so regular blood tests check kidney function.
note: Side effects page: long-term use can affect kidneys; doctor checks with blood tests.

sentence: Yellow skin or yellow whites of the eyes may signal liver problems, which can be harder to see on brown or black skin; the NHS says to call a doctor or NHS 111 straight away.
note: Side effects page: yellow skin/eyes, may be harder to see on brown or black skin; call doctor or 111 now.

sentence: A serious allergic reaction to losartan is rare.
note: Side effects page: serious allergic reaction is rare (search summary says serious effects rare).

sentence: The NHS says to call 999 if the lips, mouth, throat or tongue suddenly swell, if breathing is fast or difficult, or if the throat feels tight.
note: Side effects page: call 999 now if lips, mouth, throat or tongue swell, fast/difficult breathing, tight throat.

sentence: A raised, itchy rash can also be part of an allergic reaction.
note: Search summary: swollen raised itchy rash can signal serious allergic reaction.

sentence: Sudden swelling of parts of the body is called angioedema, and the NHS lists a past episode of it as a reason losartan may not be suitable.
note: Who can and cannot take: history of angioedema.

sentence: The NHS says painkillers such as ibuprofen, naproxen, diclofenac, celecoxib and etoricoxib can affect how losartan works.
note: Other medicines page (search summary): NSAIDs listed.

sentence: It also notes that other blood pressure medicines can cause problems when combined with losartan.
note: Search summary: taking with other BP medicines can cause problems.

sentence: Anyone unsure about a combination can ask a pharmacist or doctor.
note: Other medicines page directs readers to doctor or pharmacist (search summary; paraphrase).

sentence: Potassium-rich salt substitutes such as LoSalt can push blood potassium too high when mixed with losartan, which is why the NHS advises against them, and why doctors check potassium with blood tests.
note: Search summary: avoid salt substitutes such as Lo-Salt, high in potassium; doctors check potassium.

sentence: Alcohol can add to the blood pressure lowering effect and may bring on dizziness or light-headedness.
note: NHS common questions (search summary): alcohol increases BP-lowering effect, dizzy or light-headed.

sentence: The NHS says losartan is not recommended in pregnancy and that anyone who becomes pregnant while taking it should talk to a doctor straight away.
note: Pregnancy page (search summary): not recommended in pregnancy; if pregnant talk to doctor straight away.

sentence: It also advises that people able to become pregnant use contraception while taking it.
note: Search summary: use contraception if taking losartan.

sentence: For breastfeeding, the NHS says it might be suitable, but advice should be sought first from a doctor or pharmacist.
note: Search summary: might be OK while breastfeeding; talk to doctor or pharmacist first.

sentence: Other groups the NHS lists as unable to take it include people with a history of angioedema or with liver problems.
note: Who can and cannot take (search summary): severe heart failure, liver problems, angioedema history, low blood pressure.

sentence: During severe diarrhoea or vomiting, the NHS says to contact a doctor or pharmacist, who may advise pausing losartan until eating and drinking are back to normal.
note: Common questions (search summary): contact doctor/pharmacist; may stop until better and eating and drinking normally.

sentence: The common side effects the NHS lists for losartan are dizziness, tiredness, headache, tummy pain, feeling or being sick, and swelling of the legs, ankles or feet.
note: Search summary of the NHS common side effects list; cough was not among those returned.

sentence: Anyone with a symptom they link to the medicine can raise it with a pharmacist or doctor.
note: Absence of cough in returned list; advice to discuss is a paraphrase of NHS side-effect guidance.

sentence: Sudden swelling of the lips, mouth, throat or tongue is treated as an emergency.
note: NHS: call 999 now.

sentence: The NHS says to call 999, and not to drive to A&E oneself.
note: Search summary: NHS advises against driving yourself to A&E.

sentence: Past angioedema, meaning earlier sudden swelling of this kind, is also a reason losartan may not be suitable for a person.
note: Who can and cannot take.

sentence: The NHS lists painkillers such as ibuprofen, naproxen and diclofenac among the medicines that can affect how losartan works.
note: Search summary of other medicines page.

sentence: It also says other blood pressure medicines can cause problems alongside losartan.
note: Search summary of other medicines page.

sentence: A pharmacist or doctor can be asked which pain relief suits an individual.
note: Other medicines page directs readers to pharmacist or doctor (paraphrase).

sentence: Losartan can affect the kidneys with long-term use, and it can raise potassium in the blood.
note: Side effects: kidneys; other medicines: potassium.

sentence: Blood tests let the doctor check kidney function and potassium levels, so that any change is picked up early, and the NHS describes these checks as a routine part of treatment.
note: Doctors check kidney function and potassium with blood tests.

sentence: Alcohol can add to the blood pressure lowering effect of losartan.
note: Search summary of common questions.

sentence: That may lead to dizziness or light-headedness, and the NHS suggests taking particular care with alcohol in the first days of treatment or after the amount has been increased, when dizziness is already more likely.
note: NHS suggests avoiding alcohol in first days or after an increase (search summary).

note: NHS: call 999 now.
